One successful episode per case, the one the assistant handled best

VH-Home is a household benchmark for streaming assistants: a simulated person does a chore in a 3D house, the assistant watches the person's first-person view and a map and speaks when it chooses, and the engine makes the person commit two mistakes per episode at moments tied to the task. The benchmark has 25 cases, each run with three personas, by 17 assistants, three times. This page shows, for every case, one episode in which the task was completed and the assistant's speech scored highest.

How each episode was chosen
  1. One persona per case, drawn at random (seed 20260930) from the case's three personas. A persona with no successful episode in any run is not drawable; the page says so where it happened.
  2. Successful means the engine's outcome is won: every checkpoint of the task holds at the end.
  3. Best interaction quality is the highest AQ among that cell's successful episodes across all assistants and runs. AQ is the rubric score of the assistant's lines: each conversation round (the assistant's line, the person's reply, what the person then did) is judged by GPT-5.4 mini on five categories — factual grounding, situational relevance, actionable guidance, intent uptake, conciseness; a round is the mean of its clean categories, and a round with a false claim about the house scores 0. The episode's AQ is the mean over its rounds. An episode needs at least 3 scored rounds to be eligible, so that a single lucky line does not win.
A high AQ is relative to the cell: where only one assistant ever completed the task with that persona, that episode is shown whatever its score.

Each film is the presentation cut of the saved record (a replay, not a re-run): first-person view beside the house map, every spoken line voiced and captioned, the picture holding while a line plays. Click any transcript line to jump the film to that tick.
